Proves AR-6's `eq` operator on a `string` field, compiled case-insensitively by default (SEM-1) so it agrees with AG Grid's client-side row model. Per SEM-1's pinned collation-vs-pattern-match split, the case-insensitive comparison uses a **collation**, never `ILIKE` (reusing `ILIKE` for exact match is the escaping trap SEM-1 rules out): a `craticula_ci` collation on Postgres, a query-level `collation: {locale, strength: 2}` on Mongo, `term`/`case_insensitive` on Search. Also exercises AG-1's legacy `condition1`/`condition2`/`operator` combined-filter wire shape (pre-v29), combining two `eq` conditions with `OR` — both the legacy and current combined forms MUST parse identically per AG-1, and this is one of the fixtures pinning the legacy form.
